description.narrative:
In Southeast Nigeria, LGBTQI+ youth face violence, discrimination, and denial of services, with over 352 cases reported since 2020.Existing data doesn’t reflect their lived experiences, and the community lacks the skills to collect them. This project trains the youth-led Southeast Human Rights Coalition in Participatory Action Research (PAR) so they can safely collect and analyze their own experiences. The findings will be turned into a clear policy brief to push for changes, including amending the National Youth Policy to protect LGBTQI+ youth from discrimination and ensuring healthcare providers treat them fairly and equally through direct youth-led engagements with national and state institutions.
Over 12 months, the project will reach 76 LGBTQI youth and key institutions across Southeast Nigeria.
With a budget of €10,000, this project empowers LGBTQI+ youth, builds sustainable advocacy skills, and creates a permanent digital evidence base to drive lasting policy and social change.
The project goal is to strengthen LGBTQI+ youth-ledHuman Rights Coalition advocacy in Southeast Nigeria.
It seeks: to train 16 coalition members in participatory qualitative research and ethical documentation; to document the lived experiences of 60 LGBTQI+ youth through 10 focused Group Discussions; and; to advocate for inclusive reforms by presenting these recommendations in targeted meetings with at least 3 key stakeholders by month 8. Key activities include a 3-day Participatory Action Research (PAR) residential training, community-led data collection, development ofa policy brief, and targeted advocacy meetings with national and state institutions.

participating-org.narrative: Synergy for Health Rights and Educa

Synergy for Health Rights and Education (SHRE) is a youth-led feminist organization established to respond to systemic inequalitiesand injustices faced by marginalized communities, particularly LGBTQIA+, women, and non-binary persons, since 2020.
Rooted in principles of intersectionality, we acknowledge that feminism must address the diverse experience of those affected by race, social status, and sexuality. We are a hub for youth activism mobilizing, supporting, and amplifying the voices of marginalized young people.
SHRE envisions an inclusive society where everyone enjoys equitable healthcare, equal opportunities, and true freedom.
Our mission is to empower collective action to advance healthcare, rights, and safety for marginalized communities through advocacy, partnerships, and capacity building.
Our objectives:
To enhance access to healthcare delivery on HIV/AIDS and STIs to vulnerable people in rural and urban areas.
Sustainability and improving availability of healthcare commodities to the vulnerable communities.
Promote aninclusive policy that reduces/eliminates bias based on people's ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, nationality, gender, and identity or gender expression through sensitization, capacity building, and advocacy.
To provide a safe space for vulnerable populations who are victims of stigma and discrimination.
To support human centered researches, survey and documentaries.
Core Values:
Intersectionality
Innovation and Result-Oriented
Empowerment
Integrity
Collaboration
Equity, Feminism, and Inclusion
